assessmentSpecification: W021.5 India Post Geography & PIN Code Boundary Technical Assessment
directive: CTO Directive 148 / Workstream C / Task EB-03
governingAuthority: Master Execution Framework Amendment v1.6 / Rule IV-001 Non-Self-Acceptance

externalDatasetInvestigated.title: All India PIN Code Boundary geo-json
externalDatasetInvestigated.publishingAuthority: Department of Posts, Ministry of Communications, Government of India
externalDatasetInvestigated.declaredScope: Pan-India 6-digit Postal Index Number (PIN) boundary polygons

technicalEvaluation.geographicalEntityLevel: PIN Code Delivery Area (Not Postman Delivery Beat)
technicalEvaluation.finding: The dataset represents 6-digit PIN code delivery and sorting area polygons derived from delivery post offices (Head Post Offices and Sub Post Offices). It does NOT represent individual postman delivery beats.

deliveryBeatVsPinCodeDistinction.postmanDeliveryBeat: A dynamic operational route assigned to a specific postman within a delivery sub-office. Beats are defined along street networks, road segments, and postal delivery points; they do not have formal statutory cadastral boundaries and change dynamically based on mail volume and post office staffing.
deliveryBeatVsPinCodeDistinction.pinCodePolygon: A spatial approximation of the geographic service territory served by a 6-digit postal code. These are created by administrative clustering of delivery post offices, often using Voronoi/Thiessen tesselation constrained by road networks and administrative district boundaries.

statutoryElectoralBoundaryNonAlignment.finding: PIN code boundaries are designed exclusively for mail sorting, routing, and logistics. They are completely independent of statutory Assembly Constituencies (AC) and Parliamentary Constituencies (PC) established under the Delimitation Act.
statutoryElectoralBoundaryNonAlignment.containmentFailureInUrbanCenters: In dense metropolitan areas, a single 6-digit PIN code delivery zone routinely spans across 2, 3, or more Assembly Constituencies. Conversely, a single Assembly Constituency routinely encompasses portions of multiple PIN codes.

conclusionsAndArchitecturalRules.rule1_noArbitrarySingleAcMapping: A PIN code MUST NOT be stored as a 1:1 foreign key to an Assembly Constituency in the relational database. Doing so causes spatial misrepresentation for citizens residing in multi-AC postal zones.
conclusionsAndArchitecturalRules.rule2_failClosedCivicResolution: When a citizen provides only a 6-digit PIN code that intersects multiple ACs, the application must require secondary spatial disambiguation (e.g. locality, street, landmark, or electoral roll part number).
conclusionsAndArchitecturalRules.rule3_postalBeatDatasetNonNecessity: Because postman delivery beats are operational logistics routes that do not align with statutory electoral units, acquiring physical paper postman beat maps is NOT a valid prerequisite for statutory electoral truth. The authoritative statutory link for voters is the Polling Station / Part Number (EB-05).

disposition.recommendedAction: Classify EB-03 as a postal logistics dataset rather than a statutory electoral determinant. Transition sub-AC citizen matching to Polling Station Part Crosswalks (EB-05).
